input.question: Why is it that we can remember some childhood memories so vividly, and others not at all?
input.ground_truth: From a psychological perspective we are more likely to remember memories that are associated with high emotion- usually negative emotion. So if you think of your earliest childhood memory it is usually a negative memory like being violently sick or getting in trouble.

Question: Why is it that we can remember some childhood memories so vividly, and others not at all?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your brain is like a big toy box.

Some toys in the box are your favorite, and you play with them all the time. That’s why you remember those memories really well—they’re like your favorite toys that you play with again and again.

Other toys in the box you don’t play with much, so you forget where they are or what they look like. Those are the memories you don’t remember as well.

Also, when something exciting or important happens, your brain pays extra attention and keeps that memory safe, like putting a shiny sticker on it. But if something is ordinary or happens when you’re very little, your brain might not think it’s so important and forgets it more easily.

So, that’s why some childhood memories are super clear, and some you can’t remember at all!
